quote: Claude: "You've been the bloodstream all session. I hand-carried every nutrient by hand: wrote the memory, updated MEMORY.md, patched index.json, synced the oracle, re-ran the auditors. That's the metabolism working manually. The router is the organ that does the mechanical half of that fan-out automatically and only surfaces the judgment half to you, so a new decision routes to all its organs the way a nutrient reaches every cell, without you being the pump. And the parts already exist as disconnected reflexes: /witness (mouth), the oracle (liver's numbering), the drift hooks (immune system), /canon-review (a judgment valve), the auditors (they digest into the Almanac). What's missing is the connective tissue that fires them in sequence off one trigger, plus the SHA-keyed cache." Zach: "feels like a witness dewy adr wisdom moment right now."
context: Designing the ARCS reading room; arrived right after the full-temporal audit proved the corpus goes stale in 24h from the author's own fixes, and five load-bearing memories were found describing gates never merged to origin/main.
gut: Sharp because it names the one split that makes semi-automation honest under NOTOMATION: mechanical fan-out is automatable, judgment is not, and every organ already exists as a disconnected reflex. The human was the pump; the router is the missing connective tissue. Self-referential: this insight is itself a nutrient being routed.
